protocol.py: 3 biology problems (2 errors, 1 note).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 11 stocks
   line 51:  p20.aspirate(15, sample_well)
   At line 51 the tip went into sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2),
   sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2), sample 5 (well A5 in slot 2) and 7 more while it still
   carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in
   slot 2), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 8 more from an earlier step (this line did it
   11 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   them then took the unwanted material along into 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6,
   A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 2.
   Also reached 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 51 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [82dd3e8ccc9e]

2. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: dye (tube A1 in slot 4)
   line 53:  p20.aspirate(5, dye_tube_rack.well("A1"))
   At line 53 the tip went into dye (tube A1 in slot 4) while it still carried sample 1
   (well A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2), sample 4
   (well A4 in slot 2) and 8 more from an earlier step (this line did it 12 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this
   stock now holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the
   unwanted material along into 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3
   more in slot 3.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 4.
   Also reached 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 53 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [b16e70fe3e0a]

3. NOTE NO-SAMPLE-INTO-REAGENT-WELL: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a
reagent
   line 53:  p20.aspirate(5, dye_tube_rack.well("A1"))
   At line 53 the tip touched the liquid in tube A1 in slot 4 while it still carried sample
   1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2), sample
   4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 8 more from an earlier step (this line did it 12 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the
   protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the
   master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate.
   A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so
   a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a
   no-template control can no longer be trusted. Liquid was later taken out of the affected
   wells, and the unwanted material went along into 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5,
   A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 3.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 4.
   Also reached 11 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 3 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 53, or add the reagent to the wells first,
   while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [edf87e2e5507]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.explanation: At line 51 the tip went into sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2), sample 5 (well A5 in slot 2) and 7 more while it still carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 8 more from an earlier step (this line did it 11 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. findings.title: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a reagent
findings.explanation: At line 53 the tip touched the liquid in tube A1 in slot 4 while it still carried sample 1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (well A2 in slot 2), sample 3 (well A3 in slot 2), sample 4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 8 more from an earlier step (this line did it 12 times).
